title: Stuart Merriam v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC remanded the case to Tennessee Valley Presbytery for a new trial complying with the PCA Book of Church Order's due-process provisions; it did not decide Merriam's guilt or prohibit a new ecclesiastical trial.
first_summary: After Tennessee Valley Presbytery deposed a minister without conducting a church trial, he appealed, alleging denial of PCA due process. The SJC remanded for a new trial. It held that Presbytery could bring charges but could not substitute the Papua New Guinea criminal proceedings for ecclesiastical process, especially when it neither served an indictment and charges nor appointed counsel for an accused unable to attend. The remand permitted a constitutionally compliant trial; it did not resolve guilt or bar discipline.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Original lines 14-16 identify Stuart Merriam v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery as Case 95-10; lines 75-79 identify the appeal and SJC referral; lines 133-141 record the panel decision and approval by the SJC.
evidence_notes.dispute: Original lines 46-75 show that Presbytery charged, suspended, and then deposed Merriam through a commission without an indictment, service, plea, trial, or appointed counsel, prompting his appeal.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Original lines 85-129 hold that Presbytery denied BCO due process and require a new trial. The SJC found reliance on Papua New Guinea criminal process no substitute for a church trial and emphasized the failure to appoint counsel for an absent accused.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Original line 129 recognizes Presbytery's authority to bring charges and conduct a trial; lines 91 and 129 order a new trial, so the decision neither determines guilt nor forecloses discipline.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Not applicable; the SJC gives its own judgment and reasoning at original lines 85-129.
